articles.title: Inquest set for 88-year-old who died after well-being check by Peel police in 2023
articles.summary: An inquest will be held next week into the death of an 88-year-old man who died after he fell down a flight of stairs during a well-being check by Peel police in Mississauga nearly three years ago.

articles.title: Ontario’s new cash bail system on hold after judge grants injunction
articles.summary: Ontario’s new cash bail system has been put on hold while a judge weighs a challenge to its constitutionality. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association and the Criminal Lawyers’ Association were granted an injunction Monday, after their lawyers and those for the province presented their arguments in the case last week. articles.title: Disbarred Brampton lawyer charged in alleged $4.3M fraud scheme: Peel police
articles.summary: A disbarred Brampton lawyer has been arrested and charged with allegedly orchestrating four mortgage and cheque fraud schemes totaling around $4.3-million, Peel police say.

articles.title: Voters cast ballots in Beaches-East York federal byelection
articles.summary: Voters are heading to the polls today in the Liberal stronghold of Beaches—East York in Toronto.

articles.title: Oshawa plant adds truck as unionized Canadian GM members ratify new deals
articles.summary: The union said the three-year collective agreements increase wages for full-rate production members to $50.20 an hour and skilled trades workers to $62.71 an hour.

articles.title: Voters head to the polls for 3 federal byelections in Ontario, Quebec and B.C.
articles.summary: Voters are heading to the polls on Monday to decide three federal byelections in the B.C. riding of North Vancouver-Capilano, the Ontario riding of Beaches-East York and the Quebec riding of Chicoutimi-Le Fjord.

articles.title: Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings over decades-old, unofficial 'zone' system
articles.summary: A downtown Toronto cinema says it was forced to cancel screenings of a new movie after the film’s distributor unexpectedly withdrew access — citing a decades-old practice in Canada that limits which theatres can show movies first.
